commitResults.messageTitle: Explain a space in the email instead of listing the email rules
commitResults.messageBody:
Text after the email, such as an unknown prefix (x/what), a typo in a
prefix (adr/Blk 5) or a stray word, is read as part of the email, so
add and edit showed the long list of email format rules although the
email itself was fine (#131).

Let's check for a space first, and say that emails cannot contain
spaces, show the email as read, and list the prefixes add and edit
accept, so users can see which part of the command was not understood.

commitResults.messageTitle: Wrap long details on the contact card instead of cutting them off
commitResults.messageBody:
The name, note and projects already wrap on the contact card, but a
long company, phone, address or email was cut off with "...", even in
a maximised window, so the rest of it could not be seen anywhere in
the app (#132).

Let's let those labels wrap too. A long email with no spaces is broken
across lines as well, so the whole value is always visible.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject anything after list other than s/STATUS
commitResults.messageBody:
list ignored any other text, so list t/friends or list S/active (with
a capital S) said "Listed all contacts." and showed everyone, and a
user who meant to filter could think the filter had worked (#134). The
UG only says that help, exit and clear ignore extra text.

Let's reject other text after list with the usage message, which now
lists s/STATUS as its only parameter, and mention it in the UG.

commitResults.messageTitle: Treat tags that differ only in case as the same tag
commitResults.messageBody:
edit 1 t/Friends t/friends gave the contact two tags, Friends and
friends, which look like the same tag to a user, while names and
project names already ignore case (#136).

Let's compare tags ignoring case, so only the first one is kept, and
say so in the UG.

Phone numbers had no upper limit, so e.g. a 50-digit number was
accepted and then cut off on the contact card (#137).

Let's allow 3 to 20 digits. That is enough for an international number
with an extension, or two labelled numbers in one phone field, which
the app already accepts. The UG, the DG's manual test and the error
message now say so.

The app accepts accented names such as José María, but find only
matched them when the keyword had the same accents, so find jose or
find maria found nothing, although users often type names without
accents (#139).

Let's remove accents from both the keywords and the names and
companies before comparing them, and say so in the UG.

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain prefixes inside values and add screenshots to the UG
commitResults.messageBody:
A space followed by a prefix inside a value starts a new parameter, so
add n/Ahmad a/l Hassan saves the name Ahmad and the address l Hassan,
without any warning, and the UG did not say so (#130). Let's explain
it in the notes on the command format and in Known issues, with the
workaround: prefixes are case-sensitive, so A/L and C/O stay in the
value.

The find screenshot was still AB3's ("2 persons listed!", no sidebar),
and the UG had no screenshot of projects, the sidebar or statuses
(#140, #141). Let's retake the find screenshot and add one of the
sidebar while viewing a project, and one of list s/active.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add DG use cases for projects, roles, notes and statuses
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG had no use cases for creating or deleting a project, changing a
client's role, keeping a note, or listing clients by status, although
these are main features in the UG (#142).

Let's add them as UC10 to UC14, in the same format as the others.

commitResults.messageTitle: Acknowledge the use of AI in the DG
commitResults.messageBody:
The course's reuse policy asks teams to declare widespread use of AI
tools in the DG's Acknowledgements, saying which tool was used and how.

Let's add a "Notable uses of AI" entry for Claude, which was used to
help write code, tests and documentation, and for preliminary PR
reviews. Teammates can add their own uses to the same entry.

commitResults.messageTitle: Mark AB3 test code that the rename commit hides as unclaimed
commitResults.messageBody:
The rename commit 33ceac1f is omitted from authorship tracking, but git
did not detect two of its renames, because renaming AddressBook changed
too many of their lines: JsonAddressBookStorageTest is only 37%
similar to JsonClientBookStorageTest, and AddressBookBuilder even less
to ClientBookBuilder. Git records them as new files added in that
commit, so their AB3 lines (144 in total) were still credited to me.

Let's mark the AB3 parts of both files as unclaimed with empty
@@author tags, and mark Ryan's tests in JsonClientBookStorageTest as
his, so they stay credited to him.
